title: Apprentice commit journey map and debug rituals
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working guide for the ‘first-commit -> first-merge -> first-deploy’ path we give new SDK contributors (internal and external). Focus: make the first 60–90 minutes productive and resilient to common flubs.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: new engineers joining eng-developer-experience or platform integrators trying the SDK for the first time.
- Secondary: Solutions engineers who run pairing sessions with customers.
- Not covered: in-depth CI/CD infra design (see linked_artifacts).

Success metrics (how we know this helped):
- New contributor reaches an authored test commit in <= 90 minutes in 75% of onboarding sessions.
- Number of rollbacks caused by first-week PRs <= 5% of new contributor PRs.
- Time-to-first-merge (median) decreases by 30% vs baseline.

High-level flow (the map):
1) Preflight (5–10m): account + credentials, sandbox token, local env check.
2) Hello loop (10–20m): run a tiny example that calls the hosted API or local stub, see streaming output.
3) Tiny change (15–30m): add a second test case or tweak behavior and commit.
4) Run tests & quick lint, open PR with description template.
5) Pair review ritual (as-needed): 15–30m review with mentor, guidance on telemetry/telemetry labels.
6) Merge and smoke deploy: ensure a single synthetic smoke test passes.

Essential preflight checklist (copy into a template email/Slack DM):
- [ ] Redwood credentials provisioned (notes: check org access; ask infra if not).
- [ ] Local SDK repo cloned and checkout to onboarding branch.
- [ ] Node/Python runtime version matches .nvmrc or pyenv.
- [ ] Sandbox API key available and loaded into env var: REDWOOD_TEST_KEY.
- [ ] Dev proxy / local stubs running (./scripts/start-stub) OR note: use --remote for hosted call.

Hello loop example (one-liner explanations to run during pairing):
- Python: python examples/basic_chat.py --api-key $REDWOOD_TEST_KEY
- JS: node examples/hello_stream.js --key=$REDWOOD_TEST_KEY
Notes to mentor: show streaming output first, then explain the request/response shape and where to add a second test.

First-change recipe (what to commit):
- Add a new example file under examples/fast-path that demonstrates a tiny variation (different prompt or an embeddings call).
- Add a unit test that asserts the stubbed response shape (not content) and runs in < 1s.
- Update README snippet: one sentence about new example.
- Commit message guidance: "docs(samples): add fast-path greeting example + test".

Debug rituals (for first 5 classes of failures):
A) Broken auth / 401s
  - Quick check: echo $REDWOOD_TEST_KEY | wc -c (non-empty)
  - If using vault/KMS, check token TTL: vault token lookup or ask infra.
B) Slow streaming or timeouts
  - Reproduce with curl / --no-stream to see where server hangs.
  - Check local proxy logs: ./logs/proxy.log (tail -n 200).
C) Flaky tests (non-deterministic)
  - Is network flakiness causing it? Run tests with --repeat=10 to repro.
  - Swap to local stub to isolate infra vs logic.
D) Lint / formatting failures
  - Run pre-commit hooks: npx lint-staged OR pre-commit run --all-files.
  - Add quick lintignore if onboarding example intentionally divergent, but leave a TODO.
E) CI failures on matrix jobs
  - Check job logs for environment mismatch (node version, python version).
  - If unrelated, rerun single failing job before opening PR.

Mentor checklist during pair-review (15min script):
- Confirm the contributor can explain: what changed, why the test is sufficient, and how to run locally.
- Ask them to run the failing case and narrate what they expect.
- Point out missing telemetry keys: ensure every external request has service=examples and sample_id tags.
- Ensure secrets/keys are not accidentally committed. If found, rotate key and follow secret-rotation playbook.

PR template suggestions (tiny):
- Short summary of change
- How to run locally (exact command)
- Link to smoke test or local reproduction steps
- Who reviewed (mentor)

Post-merge smoke deploy script (to run once):
- ./scripts/smoke_deploy_check.sh examples/fast-path || rollback-guidance
- Verify telemetry appears in dev console (token-level view) within 5 minutes.

Failure mode catalog (short) — useful guardrails for mentors:
- Frequent reverts: usually indicates tests not covering stateful behavior. Consider adding a deterministic seed or isolate state.
- Excessive token usage: new samples sometimes loop prompting; add conservative max_tokens and a token-usage assertion in tests.
- Emergent performance regression: add a 90th percentile latency probe to the PR if change touches runtime path.

Fast heuristics and one-off commands (notes to self):
- Run only onboarding tests: pytest tests/onboard_* -q
- Force local stub: export REDWOOD_LOCAL_STUB=1 && npm run start-example
- Bypass streaming slow path for quick test: export REDWOOD_STREAM=false

Open questions / TODOs (for product & docs team):
- Do we want a tiny onboarding badge/plugin inside the Console so first-time SDK authors can self-provision keys? TODO: sync with product-hosted-api.
- Should we add a fixed-cost sandbox quota for onboarding so early experiments don't spike org usage? Action: open jira:DE-789 (linked_artifacts).
- Add a short screencast (3–4 minutes) demonstrating the commit flow. Who owns: Hannah Brooks (collab).

Appendix: quick mentor script (30–min session plan)
- 0–5m: preflight verification and runtimes
- 5–15m: run hello loop and explain request lifecycle
- 15–30m: implement first change + run unit test
- 30–40m: open PR and walk through PR template + telemetry
- 40–60m: pair-review, merge, and run smoke deploy

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep this doc intentionally short; split deeper infra checks into infra runbook (link to confluence:DEVEXP-310).
- This is a living doc — prefer short checklist updates over long prose.

Raw links referenced:
- onboarding jira: DE-789
- GH PR template example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/456
- Confluence runbooks: confluence:DEVEXP-310

End of draft.
